role: Detector-systems / engineering readiness reviewer (practicality, scalability, QA, DAQ)
assessment:
Engineering maturity verdict: this campaign is a well-executed TRL 3-4 physics validation of the light-collection channel (proof of concept in a relevant beam environment), not a system demonstration. The physics case that emerged — the DSB:Ce channel's ~145/137 ps intrinsic at 5/7 GeV and ~75 ps (to confirm) at 9 GeV, with the ref-included constant term nearly halved vs LuAG (323/sqrt(E)+79 vs 389/sqrt(E)+138 ps; FINDINGS.md lines 561-563, 659-670) — is exactly what justifies the next engineering phase. But every system-level axis I am asked to judge is either untested or was found wanting during the campaign itself, and — critically — the caveats are honestly documented in /Users/jameswetzel/Dropbox/01_Research/HEP/RADiCAL/02_Analysis/2026-08_CERN_T10/RADiCAL_TB_T10_Aug-2026/Output/run_12/FINDINGS.md, so my job here is largely to price them, not discover them.

(1) RADIATION HARDNESS — critical, and NOT touched by this campaign. RADiCAL's raison d'etre is rad-hard EM calorimetry at FCC-hh/muon-collider doses (order MGy ionizing and 1e15-1e16 1-MeV-neq/cm^2 at shower max over lifetime). Literature ranking of the four materials, which this campaign's channel selection must be checked against: LYSO:Ce (the fixed tiles) is the best-qualified — gamma-hard to ~1 MGy with small induced absorption and hadron-qualified by CMS MTD to ~2e14 neq/cm^2; beyond ~1e15 neq the data thins even for LYSO. LuAG:Ce (garnet crystal fiber) has a solid pedigree from fiber-calorimeter R&D (LHCb SPACAL-type studies), gamma-hard to ~1 MGy-class doses. DSB:Ce glass — the campaign's timing WINNER — has by far the thinnest radiation literature: Ce-doped silicate glasses historically darken at doses where garnets are fine, published DSB:Ce hardness data extend only to tens-of-kGy-class exposures, and dose-rate/recovery behavior is essentially uncharacterized. EJ-199 plastic WLS: plastics degrade at 0.01-0.1 MGy; a plastic WLS at shower max in an FCC-hh detector is a non-starter without new chemistry, independent of the contaminant episode. The uncomfortable engineering conclusion: the channel that won on timing is the one least qualified to survive the environment the project exists for. An irradiation campaign of actual capillary ASSEMBLIES (fiber + capillary + coupling/glue + SiPM) is the single most important critical-path item, and it gates the DSB-vs-LuAG down-select — a post-irradiation LuAG that keeps 180 ps may beat a darkened DSB.

(2) SiPM OPERATION — major, demonstrated in-campaign. The cross-run gain ladder (+/-15%, consistent with a few degC hall swing at ~5%/degC; FINDINGS.md lines 488-495), the proof that MIP normalization is NOT a valid cross-run gain monitor (species + noise-estimator bias, lines 479-487), the mid-campaign +1 V bias change that reset the calibration reference (lines 210-214), and the untaped light leak doubling daytime noise via DC photocurrent (lines 388-403) together demonstrate that the system as operated has NO gain-monitoring plane at all. This is a solved problem in the field (per-channel temperature readback + bias compensation, plus LED/laser pulser injection — the log itself prescribes exactly this at line 493-494), but it must be designed in: pulser light distribution to every channel is a real mechanical/optical design constraint at 1e5-1e6 channels, not an afterthought. Until it exists, response linearity claims are capped at the +/-15% envelope — which the site correctly states (index.html, Materials card). Additionally, HG baseline RMS tracking bias raises (24-38 -> 81-111 ADC-eq, lines 252-254) previews the post-irradiation reality: SiPM dark currents grow orders of magnitude at 1e13-1e14 neq, so the real system needs active cooling and an annealing strategy for the photodetector plane — nowhere yet in the design.

(3) DYNAMIC RANGE — major, already exhausted at test-beam energies. The brightest channel (DSB1, ~1,350 ADC-eq/GeV) soft-hit the ~13.6k ADC-eq LG ceiling at 11 GeV (lines 552-556); the ceiling therefore sits at roughly a 10 GeV full-response equivalent. FCC-hh EM showers are 50 GeV to multi-TeV: the front end needs order x30-x100 more range. The dual-gain architecture is the right shape, but note the HG chain clipped 1-12% of pulses at FIVE GeV before offset retuning (lines 25-31), and the campaign spent real effort on clip-recovery analysis heroics (srCFD, wall-aware transfer fits, lines 232-243) — acceptable R&D triage, unacceptable as a design pattern. Scaling also re-opens SiPM pixel saturation, acquitted at these light levels (lines 475-477) but not at x30 photons — and the pixel budget cannot even be computed yet because the absolute photoelectron scale is only 'planned' (index.html Materials card). Separately, the 1024-sample record truncates the slow LG component at ~50% of peak (lines 54-59): integration-window design is currently mismatched to the LYSO decay.

(4) CHANNEL COUNT / COST — unquantified. 4 capillaries x dual gain = 8 waveform channels per 14x14 mm module face; any physical calorimeter is 1e5-1e6 channels. No capillary manufacturing yield, unit cost, or assembly-time data exist from this campaign. One genuinely useful NEW input: the correlated per-capillary timing discovered in DSB1 (sigma(diff)/2 exceeding the ref-included width, lines 663-667) means the 4-capillary timing gain does NOT scale as sqrt(N) in high-light channels — which argues against over-provisioning per-module timing channels and is directly relevant to the cost model, but first the correlation must be shown to be physical (shower fluctuations/position quadrupole) rather than a common-mode readout artifact.

(5) MANUFACTURING QA — the EJ-199 episode is a textbook supply-chain lesson. A spec-compliant EJ-199 (tuned for LuO:Yb, absorption excluding LYSO's 425 nm) should have been nearly blind; observed ~550-650 ADC-eq/GeV with a 6.5 ns tail is in-beam, quantified support for the Eljen-contaminant hypothesis (lines 636-641, 652-657). A beam test was used as an expensive spectrometer to discover an incoming-materials defect. For production: mandatory per-batch bench QA (absorption/emission spectra, decay-time fingerprint — the 12.5/6.5/4.9 ns tau table is exactly the right observable) before anything ships to a beam or a detector. Credit where due: the team converted the failure into a quantified fingerprint for the vendor conversation.

(6) DAQ — DRS4 is a lab instrument, not a scalable architecture, and it also set the measurement floor. The CAEN DT5742's inter-group jitter of 104.5-115 ps (lines 84, 223, 660-661) is COMPARABLE TO OR LARGER THAN the DSB1 intrinsic being claimed (~75 ps at 9 GeV): the campaign's headline number is a reference-subtracted inference sitting under the electronics floor of its own DAQ, which is why the log itself flags it 'to be confirmed with a downstream reference next beam test' (line 669). Switched-capacitor waveform digitizers have ms-scale dead time and kHz-class burst rates — fine at T10's 2-30 Hz, irrelevant at 40 MHz BX. The path to scale is a fast-timing front-end ASIC (HGCROC/ETROC/FastIC-class TOA+TOT or on-chip CFD) with <=30-50 ps electronics jitter, plus a clock-distribution system at the 10-20 ps level — without which the demonstrated sub-100 ps intrinsic constant term is unrecoverable at system level. Neither exists in the project plan as evidenced here.

Also structural, already documented but with engineering consequences: no tracker (sigma/E position-smearing dominated everywhere, intrinsic ~10% bounded exactly once at 5 GeV, lines 102-109), single module (no lateral containment, no inter-module cross-talk or dead-material data), shower-max-only sampling (this is a timing/position channel qualification, not a calorimeter qualification), and T10's 11 GeV ceiling with the standing purity caveat (open markers, lines 595-608) — the energies where the dynamic-range and saturation questions actually live require SPS (H2/H4) beams.
strengths: Operational discipline well above typical test-beam standard: uniform per-run QC/integrity pipeline (QCv2.C, ChannelIntegrity.C), per-run MIP calibration, and root-cause culture — the light leak, the gain ladder, and the apparent saturation were each run to ground (SaturationStudy.C, four-test acquittal/conviction structure, FINDINGS.md lines 468-495) instead of being absorbed into error bars.

Every major systematic I would look for as an engineer is already documented, quantified, and bounded in FINDINGS.md — the +/-15% gain envelope, the LG ceiling, the 11 GeV purity caveat, the correlated capillary timing. The review surface is honest; nothing had to be dug out.

The diagonal-difference estimator (validated: implied reference jitter 107-114 ps matching the known ~105 ps DRS + MCP budget, lines 659-662) is exactly the right methodology for a test whose DAQ jitter rivals the detector — it produced reference-free intrinsic numbers and, as a bonus, DISCOVERED the correlated capillary timing, a system-design-relevant fact.

Dual-gain readout with wall-aware clip recovery (srCFD, TransferFit.C, lines 232-243) kept the campaign productive despite dynamic-range shortfalls — the right architecture shape for the real system, exercised end-to-end.

In-situ self-diagnosis capability demonstrated: miss-fraction as a live alignment monitor (6.4 mm offset found and fixed by data, lines 149-204), MCP-threshold audits per run, in-situ beam-composition measurement that corrected the official T10 tables at 7/9/11 GeV — the instrument monitors itself, a genuinely good trait for a future system.

The EJ-199 failure was converted into a quantified, bench-comparable contaminant fingerprint (tau = 6.5 ns vs LuAG 12.5 / DSB1 4.9 ns, lines 652-657) rather than a dead dataset — the correct QA response, retroactively.

The physics result itself clears the bar to justify the next engineering phase: DSB:Ce intrinsic ~145/137 ps at 5/7 GeV with ~75 ps indicated at 9 GeV, constant term nearly halved vs LuAG, on a shashlik geometry with interchangeable light collection — a real, differentiated timing channel.
weaknesses: CRITICAL — Radiation hardness untested, and the down-select is inverted relative to radiation pedigree: the timing winner (DSB:Ce glass) is the least radiation-qualified material in the stack (glass darkening; literature ~tens of kGy vs MGy-class for LYSO/LuAG garnet), in a project whose entire premise is MGy / 1e16 neq/cm^2 survival. No irradiation data on capillary assemblies, couplings, or the SiPM plane exists. The channel choice cannot be considered made until post-irradiation timing is measured.

MAJOR — No gain-monitoring plane: no temperature logging, no optical pulser, no bias compensation; MIP normalization proven invalid as a monitor (lines 479-487). Consequence already realized: linearity is only established to +/-15% (lines 493-495), which would be a fatal constant term in a real calorimeter. This is standard engineering that simply was not present.

MAJOR — Dynamic range exhausted at 11 GeV by the brightest channel (LG ceiling ~13.6k ADC-eq, lines 552-556) and HG clipping at 5 GeV pre-retune (lines 25-31); target showers are 30-100x larger. No front-end range budget, no SiPM pixel budget (absolute pe scale not yet measured), and the campaign leaned on clip-recovery analysis to compensate.

MAJOR — DAQ electronics jitter (~105-115 ps DRS inter-group, lines 84, 660-661) is comparable to or larger than the claimed DSB1 intrinsic (~75 ps at 9 GeV): the headline number is a subtraction-based inference below the instrument's own floor, flagged 'to be confirmed' in the log itself (line 669). No scalable front-end (ASIC) or clock-distribution concept is in evidence.

MAJOR — Energy-resolution qualification structurally blocked: no tracker, so sigma/E is position-smearing dominated at every point (18-65%) with the intrinsic ~10% bounded exactly once via an edge fit (lines 102-109). Also single module, shower-max-only sampling: no containment, cross-talk, or dead-material information.

MINOR — Environmental control absent at test: untaped light leak (lines 388-403), self-heating thermal equilibrium discovered rather than designed (lines 370-376), collimator/gas-pressure configs not logged per run until it cost a night (1 GeV rate mystery, lines 497-527). All test-beam foibles, but they cost calibration continuity (run 15 reference does not carry to runs 12/14, lines 210-214).

MINOR — EJ-199 contaminated stock reached beam time with no incoming-material bench QA; the channel's dataset is a baseline for a hypothesis rather than the planned measurement (lines 613-624, 636-641).

NIT — DSB1 correlated capillary timing (lines 663-667) is currently unattributed (physical shower correlation vs common-mode readout); until resolved it clouds both the sqrt(N) channel-multiplicity assumption and the diff/2 upper-bound interpretation.
open_questions: What is DSB:Ce glass's induced absorption and timing performance after 0.1-1 MGy gamma and 1e15-1e16 neq/cm^2 — and does LuAG:Ce overtake it post-irradiation? (Gates the channel down-select; nothing in this campaign informs it.)

Where do the SiPMs sit in the real module geometry, what lifetime dose/fluence do they see, and what is the cooling + annealing plan for the photodetector plane given dark-current growth already visible from bias raises alone (lines 252-254)?

What is the absolute photoelectron yield per GeV for the DSB1 channel (dark-pulse calibration 'planned', index.html), and hence the SiPM pixel-count budget for linearity at 100-500 GeV shower-max light — x30-100 today's maximum?
What front-end architecture replaces the DRS4 — TOA/TOT ASIC vs on-chip CFD — and what clock-distribution jitter budget preserves a <100 ps constant term across 1e5-1e6 channels?

Is the DSB1 correlated per-capillary timing physical (shower fluctuations / position quadrupole) or instrumental (common-mode in the digitizer group)? A downstream independent time reference plus channel-shuffled cabling would separate them.
Can the ~75 ps DSB1 figure at 9 GeV be confirmed with a reference whose jitter is well below it (the log's own to-confirm item, line 669) — e.g., a second MCP downstream on an independent digitizer?
What are capillary fabrication yield, unit cost, and assembly time — and does the correlated-timing finding allow fewer timing channels per module without performance loss?

What beam program covers the actual operating point — SPS H2/H4 for 50-300 GeV (dynamic range, saturation, containment with a matrix of modules) and a tracker for intrinsic sigma/E — since T10 has delivered what it can at 1-11 GeV?
recommendation: Proceed to the next phase — the DSB:Ce timing result earns it — but gate the program on engineering, not more T10 statistics. Concretely, in priority order: (1) Launch the irradiation campaign NOW (gamma + hadron, on real capillary assemblies including couplings and SiPMs, for both DSB:Ce and LuAG:Ce): it is the longest-lead, highest-leverage item and it, not this beam test, decides the channel down-select for a rad-hard calorimeter. (2) Before any further beam time, install the minimum monitoring plane the log itself prescribes (line 493-494): per-channel/board temperature logging, an LED/laser pulser, light-tight enclosure verification, and frozen bias with compensation — otherwise the next campaign inherits the same +/-15% linearity ceiling. (3) Next beam test must carry a downstream independent time reference (to confirm ~75 ps and resolve the capillary-correlation question) and impact-position tagging (tracker) to finally measure intrinsic sigma/E; both are prerequisites for publishable system numbers, not upgrades. (4) Produce a dynamic-range design note — pe/GeV from the planned dark-pulse calibration, pixel budget, front-end range split — targeted at 300 GeV showers, and identify the front-end ASIC candidate and clock-distribution scheme that replace the DRS4; without these the timing result does not transfer to any real detector. (5) Institute per-batch incoming-materials bench QA (absorption/emission + decay-time fingerprint) as a standing rule — the EJ-199 episode should be the last time a beam test discovers a supply-chain defect. Classify the present result honestly in the paper: a TRL 3-4 validation of an interchangeable light-collection channel at shower max, with system-level readiness (radiation, monitoring, range, DAQ, cost) still ahead of, not behind, the collaboration.
